{{Short description|Mathematical norm}}
{{more citations needed|date=November 2013}}

In [[mathematics]], specifically [[functional analysis]], the '''[[Robert Schatten|Schatten]] norm''' (or '''Schatten–von-Neumann norm''') arises as a generalization of ''p''-integrability similar to the [[trace class]] [[norm (mathematics)|norm]] and the [[Hilbert–Schmidt operator|Hilbert–Schmidt]] norm.

==Definition==
Let <math>H_1</math>, <math>H_2</math> be Hilbert spaces, and <math>T</math> a (linear) [[bounded operator]] from 
<math>H_1</math> to <math>H_2</math>. For <math>p\in [1,\infty)</math>, define the Schatten ''p''-norm of <math>T</math> as

: <math> \|T\| _p = [\operatorname{Tr} (|T|^p)]^{1/p}, </math>
where <math>|T|:=\sqrt{(T^*T)}</math>, using the [[Square_root_of_a_matrix#Square_roots_of_positive_operators|operator square root]].

If <math>T</math> is compact and <math>H_1,\,H_2</math> are separable, then

: <math> \|T\| _p := \bigg( \sum_{n\ge 1} s^p_n(T)\bigg)^{1/p} </math>

for  <math> s_1(T) \ge s_2(T) \ge \cdots \ge s_n(T) \ge \cdots \ge 0</math> the [[singular values]] of <math>T</math>, i.e. the eigenvalues of the Hermitian operator <math>|T|:=\sqrt{(T^*T)}</math>.

=== Special cases ===

*The Schatten 1-norm is the '''[[nuclear norm]]''' (also known as the '''[[trace norm]]''', or the '''[[Singular Value Decomposition#Ky Fan norms|Ky Fan]] ''n''-norm'''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fan |first=Ky. |date=1951 |title=Maximum properties and inequalities for the eigenvalues of completely continuous operators |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=37 |issue=11 |pages=760–766 |bibcode=1951PNAS...37..760F |doi=10.1073/pnas.37.11.760 |pmc=1063464 |pmid=16578416 |doi-access=free}}</ref>).
* The Schatten 2-norm is the '''[[Frobenius norm]]'''.
* The Schatten ∞-norm is the '''[[spectral norm]]''' (also known as the '''operator norm''', or the largest singular value).

==Properties==
In the following we formally extend the range of <math> p </math> to <math>[1,\infty]</math> with the convention that <math> \|\cdot\|_{\infty} </math> is the operator norm. The dual index to <math>p=\infty</math> is then <math>q=1</math>.

* The Schatten norms are unitarily invariant: for unitary operators <math> U </math> and <math> V </math> and <math>p\in [1,\infty]</math>,

:: <math> \|U T V\|_p = \|T\|_p. </math>

* They satisfy [[Hölder's inequality]]: for all <math> p\in [1,\infty]</math> and <math>q</math> such that <math>\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1</math>, and operators <math> S\in\mathcal{L}(H_2,H_3), T\in\mathcal{L}(H_1,H_2)</math> defined between Hilbert spaces <math>H_1, H_2, </math> and <math> H_3</math> respectively,
:: <math> \|ST\|_1 \leq \|S\|_p \|T\|_q. </math>
If <math>p,q,r\in [1,\infty]</math> satisfy <math>\tfrac{1}{p} + \tfrac{1}{q} = \tfrac{1}{r}</math>, then we have
:: <math>\|ST\|_r \leq \|S\|_p \|T\|_q</math>.
The latter version of Hölder's inequality is proven in higher generality (for noncommutative <math>L^p</math> spaces instead of Schatten-p classes) in.<ref name="Fock and Kosaki">{{cite journal |last1=Fack |first1=Thierry |last2=Kosaki |first2=Hideki |title=Generalized <math>s</math>-numbers of <math>\tau</math>-measurable operators. |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |date=1986 |volume=123 |issue=2 |url=https://msp.org/pjm/1986/123-2/pjm-v123-n2-p03-s.pdf}}</ref>
(For matrices the latter result is found in<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1007/BF01231769|title = Sharp uniform convexity and smoothness inequalities for trace norms|journal = Inventiones Mathematicae|volume = 115|pages = 463–482|year = 1994|last1 = Ball|first1 = Keith|last2 = Carlen|first2 = Eric A.|last3 = Lieb|first3 = Elliott H.| bibcode=1994InMat.115..463B |s2cid = 189831705}}</ref>.)

* Sub-multiplicativity: For all <math> p\in [1,\infty]</math> and operators <math> S\in\mathcal{L}(H_2,H_3), T\in\mathcal{L}(H_1,H_2)</math> defined between Hilbert spaces <math>H_1, H_2, </math> and <math> H_3</math> respectively,

:: <math> \|ST\|_p \leq \|S\|_p \|T\|_p .</math>

* Monotonicity: For <math> 1\leq p\leq p'\leq\infty</math>,

:: <math> \|T\|_1 \geq \|T\|_p \geq \|T\|_{p'} \geq \|T\|_\infty. </math>

* Duality: Let <math>H_1, H_2</math> be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, <math> p\in [1,\infty]</math> and <math>q</math> such that <math>\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1</math>, then

:: <math> \|S\|_p = \sup\lbrace |\langle S,T\rangle | \mid \|T\|_q = 1\rbrace, </math>

: where <math>\langle S,T\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(S^*T) </math> denotes the [[Hilbert–Schmidt inner product]].

*Let <math> (e_k)_k,(f_{k'})_{k'}</math> be two orthonormal basis of the Hilbert spaces <math>H_1, H_2</math>, then for <math> p=1</math>

:: <math> \|T\|_1 \leq \sum_{k,k'}\left|T_{k,k'}\right|. </math>

==Remarks==

Notice that <math>\|\cdot\|_2 </math> is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (see [[Hilbert–Schmidt operator]]), <math>\|\cdot\|_1 </math> is the trace class norm (see [[trace class]]), and <math>\|\cdot\|_\infty</math> is the operator norm (see [[operator norm]]).

Note that the [[Matrix norm|matrix p-norm]] is often also written as <math>\|\cdot\|_p</math>, but it is not the same as Schatten norm. In fact, we have <math>\|A\|_{\text{matrix p-norm}, 2} = \|A\|_{\text{Schatten}, \infty}</math>.

For <math>p\in(0,1)</math> the function <math>\|\cdot\|_p</math> is an example of a [[quasinorm]].

An operator which has a finite Schatten norm is called a [[Schatten class operator]] and the space of such operators is denoted by <math> S_p(H_1,H_2)</math>. With this norm, <math> S_p(H_1,H_2)</math> is a [[Banach space]], and a Hilbert space for ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2.

Observe that <math> S_p(H_1,H_2) \subseteq \mathcal{K} (H_1,H_2)</math>, the algebra of [[compact operator]]s. This follows from the fact that if the sum is finite the spectrum will be finite or countable with the origin as [[Accumulation point|limit point]], and hence a compact operator (see [[compact operator on Hilbert space]]).
